_comment: THE INSTALL SITE'S ENVIRONMENTS (#231).
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DECIDE, and deliberately so:
· the HOSTNAME. A unit's public DN is DERIVED per environment by gov from `app_domain` plus
the base domain — prod is bare, every other env carries `-<env>` (svm-prj-work:
knowledge/deployment/specs/public-dn-convention.md, ratified PRJ-43 2026-07-28). Listing
hosts here would be a second copy of a derived fact, which is the two-copies-never-compared
pattern. `dn` below is what gov derives, recorded ONLY so the built page can print it.
· the CLIENT VERSION for a deploy. `gov-cicd deploy` owns per-env pins in
catalog/pins.yaml and `--promote <from> <to>` copies them env to env (build-once-promote).
INTERIM: prod is on gov.svayamtech.com, not gov.svayam.ai. The DN convention hardcodes the
apex, so a second SLD is not expressible yet — Svayamtech/910-GOV-CICD#273 requests
app_domain + base_domain, and that issue also carries the `former_domains` redirect requirement
so the eventual switch keeps old links working. Change `base` here when #273 lands.
PRERELEASE CHANNELS DO NOT EXIST YET. The published package carries exactly one dist-tag
(latest -> 1.2.2): no next, no uat, no dev. So uat and dev pin the SAME client as prod and
differ only in the SCRIPT ref. They can diverge the moment a prerelease channel is published;
pinning them at a channel that does not exist would fail with `No matching version found`.
PROD PINS TWO IMMUTABLE THINGS (2026-09-17). The CLIENT is 1.2.2, which npm stamps as built from
c05aa80 — the Policy Owner's pin for 1.2.2. That commit has NO install.sh (the installer landed
later), so the SCRIPT ref is a full `main` commit that carries the fetch-then-run installer.
From 1.2.3 onward both are one gov release tag: set prod.ref to `gov-work-<semver>` once
`gov promote gov-work --to prod` has cut it (Svayamtech/910-GOV-CICD#274), and add that tag
to `versioned`. 1.2.2 has no versioned pair: a release with no installer of its own has none to serve.

uat.label: UAT — release candidate. Not the version to adopt.

dev.label: DEV — the tip of the dev branch. Expect it to be broken.
